cues: Julia de Burgos was born in nineteen fourteen in Puerto Rico, the eldest of thirteen children in a very poor family; six of her brothers and sisters died of malnutrition.
She became a teacher at twenty one, and a nationalist: for her, independence for the island, dignity for the poor and freedom for women were one cause.
This poem comes from her first book, from nineteen thirty eight.
She later lived in New York and Cuba, and died in poverty in Spanish Harlem in nineteen fifty three.
Today she is a national figure, and a forerunner of Latina writers.
